rounds.text: Concerns regarding Nexus Surgical and Medicare Ltd begin with severe governance and ownership red flags, specifically a low promoter holding of just 18.73% [E34, E52]. The operational stability of the firm is also questionable, marked by an inconsistent yearly operating-margin trend over the last three years [E25] and a contraction in operating margin from 14% down to 12% by Mar 2026 [E23]. Furthermore, a significant disconnect exists between reported earnings and actual cash generation, highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.23x where operating cash flow represents only 18% of operating profit for Mar 2026 [E27, E30]. Historical performance compounds these fundamental risks, demonstrated by a 10-year compounded share price growth of -10% [E16] and an extreme historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -96.5% alongside a negligible Sharpe ratio of 0.04 [E44, E46]. Conceded: the company maintains zero debt [E31], strong multi-year sales and profit growth [E8, E13], and high returns on equity [E7].
